prompt: In WCAG 2.2, which layer is the one a test passes or fails?
hint: A guideline has no level of its own.

choices.text: The four principles, known together as POUR
choices.why: The principles organise the rest; nothing is tested against "perceivable" directly.

choices.text: The thirteen guidelines, such as 1.4 Distinguishable
choices.why: A guideline is a goal with no pass or fail of its own.

choices.text: The success criteria, numbered like 2.1.1 Keyboard
choices.why: Right. Each has a number, a level and a sentence a page meets or does not.

choices.text: The techniques the W3C publishes alongside them
choices.why: Techniques are ways to meet a criterion, informative rather than required; failing to use one is not a failure.

prompt: Put WCAG's four principles in the order of their numbers, 1 to 4.
A booking flow has three pages. Two meet every A and AA criterion; the payment page fails one AA criterion. What can be claimed?
hint: A process is judged as a whole.

choices.text: AA for the flow, since two pages out of three conform
choices.why: There is no majority rule: one failing page in a process fails the process.

choices.text: Level A for the flow, and not AA
choices.why: Right. Every page meets A, so the flow conforms at A; the payment page keeps it from AA.

choices.text: AA for the two pages and for the flow, with the payment page listed as an exception
choices.why: The pages may be claimed alone, but a flow with a failing step cannot be.

choices.text: Nothing at all, because one criterion failed
choices.why: The failure is at AA; level A is still met on every page.

prompt: Which of these success criteria were added in WCAG 2.2? Choose all that apply.
hint: Nine were added; one was removed.

choices.text: 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)
choices.why: Right. 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or that much space around the target.

choices.text: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)
choices.why: That one is from WCAG 2.0.

choices.text: 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
choices.why: Right. The focused control may not be entirely hidden by something the page drew.

choices.text: 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast
choices.why: That one came with WCAG 2.1, in 2018.

choices.text: 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
choices.why: Right. Signing in may not hinge on a memory or transcription test without another way.

prompt: An audit report written against WCAG 2.1 lists a failure of 4.1.1 Parsing. What does it mean for a WCAG 2.2 requirement?

choices.text: It is a level A failure, so the page fails 2.2 at every level
choices.why: It would be, in 2.1. 2.2 no longer has the criterion.

choices.text: It moves to level AAA in 2.2, so an AA claim is safe
choices.why: It did not move; it was removed.

choices.text: 2.2 no longer tests it, so there it decides nothing at all
choices.why: Right. 4.1.1 was removed because browsers repair broken markup the same way.

choices.text: The report is invalid and the whole audit has to be redone
choices.why: The other findings still apply: 2.2 contains 2.1's criteria apart from this one.

prompt: Why is AA, and not AAA, the level most requirements name?
hint: Where does the requirement usually come from?

choices.text: Laws and procurement standards point at AA, and the W3C advises against AAA for whole sites
choices.why: Right. A team inherits AA from a contract or a regulation.

choices.text: AAA criteria have no machine checks, so nobody can test them
choices.why: Many AA criteria have none either; testing by hand is ordinary.

choices.text: AAA is a separate standard that replaces AA
choices.why: The levels nest: AAA includes everything at A and AA.

choices.text: AA was the last level to be published
choices.why: All three levels have existed since WCAG 2.0.

prompt: Match each rule to the way it reaches WCAG.
hint: Three of the four name a version somewhere.

pairs.right: through EN 301 549, which carries WCAG 2.1 AA
WCAG 2.0 A and AA, by reference
guidelines adopted internationally, no version named
built on WCAG 2.0, for government sites

right_distractors: WCAG 2.2 AAA for every private website

prompt: A team must satisfy Section 508 (WCAG 2.0 AA) and EN 301 549 (WCAG 2.1 AA). Which single target covers both?
hint: Each version contains the one before it.

choices.text: WCAG 2.0 AA, because it is the version both laws share
choices.why: 2.0 lacks the criteria 2.1 added, so EN 301 549 would not be met.

choices.text: WCAG 2.2 AA
choices.why: Right. 2.2 AA contains 2.1 AA and 2.0 AA.

choices.text: WCAG 2.1 A, plus whatever 2.0 AA adds to it
choices.why: That leaves out the AA criteria 2.1 added, such as 1.4.11.

choices.text: Two separate test plans, one per version
choices.why: Possible, and wasted: one plan at 2.2 AA answers both.

prompt: Match each defect in book.html to the success criterion it fails.
hint: The notes beside the page name them.

pairs.left: an empty name only turns the border red

prompt: Why does a functional test of book.html pass, with all eight defects in place?
hint: How does such a test press Book?

choices.text: Functional tests skip any page that is served as a static file
choices.why: Nothing about a static file stops a browser test from opening it.

choices.text: It clicks, reads the screen, and the seat gets booked
choices.why: Right. The defects only show for somebody without a mouse or without sight of the screen.

choices.text: The defects are in the CSS, which tests do not load
choices.why: A browser test loads the CSS; and most defects are in the markup.

choices.text: POST /bookings has no defect, and that is what it checks
choices.why: A browser test goes through the page, and the page is where the defects are; but it goes through as a mouse user who can see.

prompt: The Book control is a <div> with onclick. What does a keyboard user meet?

choices.text: A button they can reach, but whose name is not read out
choices.why: They cannot reach it at all; a <div> is not in the tab order.

choices.text: A control that works with Enter but not with Space
choices.why: Neither key reaches it, because it never has the focus.

choices.text: Nothing to press, so no way to book
choices.why: Right. It fails 2.1.1 Keyboard, and 4.1.2 because it has no role either.

choices.text: A working control, since the browser adds keyboard support to any element with onclick
choices.why: Browsers add nothing; only native controls, or elements given tabindex and key handlers, answer the keyboard.

prompt: What contrast ratio did contrast.py print for #767676 on white? Give the first number of the ratio, to two decimals.
hint: It is the lightest grey that passes AA on white.

prompt: For ordinary text at level AA, 1.4.3 asks for a contrast ratio of at least ___ to 1.
The error border in book.html is #dd0000 on white, 5.15:1. Is defect 8 fixed by that number?

choices.text: Yes: it passes 1.4.11's 3:1, so the error is perceivable
choices.why: It is visible, and it is still only a colour, which is what 1.4.1 forbids.

choices.text: No: contrast passes, but the error is still carried by colour alone
choices.why: Right. 1.4.11 and 1.4.1 are separate criteria; meeting one says nothing about the other.

choices.text: No: a border needs 4.5:1, like text
choices.why: A border is not text; 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of it.

choices.text: Yes, provided it also passes 7:1 for AAA
choices.why: AAA is not the requirement here, and contrast is not the defect.

prompt: A designer proposes 18-pixel bold text in #949494 on white, about 3.0:1. Does it meet 1.4.3 at AA?
hint: Large text is 14 point bold, about 18.7 pixels.

choices.text: Yes, because bold text counts as large at any size
choices.why: Bold lowers the size threshold to 14 point; it does not remove it.

choices.text: No: it falls just short of large, so 4.5:1 applies
choices.why: Right. 14 point is about 18.7 pixels, so 18 is ordinary text and 3.0:1 fails.

choices.text: Yes: 3:1 is the AA threshold for all bold text
choices.why: 3:1 is for large text, and bold is large only from 14 point.

choices.text: Only at AAA, which asks 4.5:1 for large text
choices.why: True of AAA, but the question is about AA, and this text is not large.

prompt: A login page asks the user to type the six characters shown in a distorted image, with no other way in. Which WCAG 2.2 criterion is the clearest failure?
hint: It is new in 2.2, and it is about signing in.

choices.text: 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)
choices.why: Nothing here is about the size of what is clicked.

choices.text: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)
choices.why: Contrast may fail too, but a perfect-contrast puzzle is still a puzzle.

choices.text: 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
choices.why: Right. Transcribing characters is a cognitive test, and there is no alternative.

choices.text: 3.2.6 Consistent Help
choices.why: That is about where help sits across pages.

prompt: A team fixes book.html until every criterion at A and AA is met, then is asked by a public client for AAA. What should the tester say first?
hint: What does the W3C say about AAA for whole sites?

choices.text: That AAA is the same as AA with stricter contrast
choices.why: Contrast is one of 31 further criteria, not the only difference.

choices.text: That conforming at AA already implies AAA for a page this simple
choices.why: AA implies nothing about the AAA criteria; each one is checked.

choices.text: That AAA cannot be tested, so it cannot be written into a contract
choices.why: AAA criteria are testable like any other; some content just cannot meet them.

choices.text: Which AAA criteria suit its users and its content
choices.why: Right. The W3C advises against AAA as a blanket target and for choosing AAA criteria where they fit.
